incidente.resumo: For a short period in October, the Xubuntu download page served a malicious zip file instead of the expected torrents after a malicious actor brute-forced a vulnerable component of the Canonical-maintained WordPress installation and injected code that changed the download links. Canonical locked down the site and disabled the downloads page, then worked to remove the malicious code, roll back affected pages and harden WordPress; by October 19 the malicious file was confirmed removed and the site considered clean.

descricao.texto: The compromise was first reported on October 15; the community reported it in multiple places (Reddit, Matrix, IRC) and raised multiple tickets with Canonical, whose infrastructure and security teams were alerted shortly afterward.
trechos:

passos.texto: Between October 15 and October 19, the Canonical team worked to identify the access method, remove all malicious code and injected files, roll back the affected pages to a verified clean state, and harden the WordPress instance; by October 19 community members confirmed the malicious zip file had been removed and the site was considered clean.
trechos: Between October 15 and October 19, the Canonical team worked to:
- Identify the method used to obtain unauthorized access,
- Remove all malicious code and injected files,
- Roll back the affected pages to a verified clean state, and
- Harden the WordPress instance to safeguard against further intrusion.

By October 19, community members confirmed that the malicious zip file
had been removed and that the site was considered clean.

acoes.texto: Already done: according to Canonical's November 11 incident summary, the exploit path was addressed, the system hardened, and download access restored in a controlled, read-only mode to allow migration to a new static site.
trechos:
On November 11, Canonical provided the Xubuntu team with an incident
summary confirming that the exploit path had been addressed, the
system had been hardened, and that download access had been restored
in a controlled, read-only mode to allow migration to a new static
site.

acoes.texto: The team decided to switch the website to Hugo, a static site generator, which it says will completely eliminate this type of attack vector; launch is planned soon.
trechos:
The biggest announcement is that we’ve decided to switch to Hugo, a
static site generator which will completely eliminate the type of
attack vector taken advantage of.

observacoes: The year in data_incidente comes from the message date (Mon Nov 17 2025), which refers to the compromise as "last month" (October). categoria_causa is other: the text says a vulnerable WordPress component was brute forced but states neither a credential weakness nor a code defect. The text says only the website and its torrent links were impacted; cdimages.ubuntu.com, official repositories, build systems and packages were not. The document is a post-mortem posted to the xubuntu-users mailing list. Advice to affected users (not a prevention measure): anyone who downloaded or opened "Xubuntu-Safe-Download.zip" should assume it was malicious, scan their computer with antivirus or anti-malware software and delete the file.
